name: Land contamination risk management (LCRM)
fact: Environment Agency LCRM sets the staged framework for assessing and managing risks from historic land contamination; page last updated 12 June 2025.
gate: Framework guidance is not site evidence; exact contaminant linkages, investigation and verification remain required.

name: LCRM: Before you start
fact: LCRM separates risk assessment, options appraisal, remediation and verification into distinct stages and requires competent-person input.
gate: Completion of an earlier stage does not prove remediation or verification is complete.

name: LCRM: Stage 1 risk assessment
fact: Stage 1 requires a preliminary risk assessment, conceptual site model and tiered quantitative assessment; intrusive investigation may be required.
gate: Desk-study or map risk alone is not an intrusive site investigation or confirmed contaminant linkage.

name: LCRM: Stage 2 options appraisal
fact: Stage 2 requires feasible remediation options to be identified, evaluated and selected against site-specific objectives and current information.
gate: Selecting an option is not proof remediation was implemented or verified.

name: LCRM: Stage 3 remediation and verification
fact: Stage 3 separates remediation strategy, implementation, verification report and any long-term monitoring or maintenance.
gate: Remediation works claimed or started are not equivalent to a verified suitable-for-use site.

name: Voluntary remediation advice for contaminated land and groundwater
fact: Environment Agency guidance published 3 June 2026 offers site-specific regulatory advice where land contamination has impacted controlled waters.
gate: Seeking or receiving advice is not regulatory approval, planning discharge or verification of remediation.

name: Land affected by contamination planning guidance
fact: National planning guidance treats contamination as a material planning issue and uses the suitable-for-use approach for development.
gate: Planning policy context does not establish that a target site is contaminated or remediated.

name: Land contamination technical guidance collection
fact: Environment Agency technical guidance collection was updated 13 May 2026 and links risk, planning, Part 2A, groundwater, gases, remediation and regulatory-control resources.
gate: A guidance collection is discovery context and not parcel-level environmental evidence.

name: Contaminated land statutory guidance
fact: Defra statutory guidance explains how local authorities determine contaminated land in the legal Part 2A sense and how remediation provisions apply.
gate: Presence of contaminants or a historic use is not automatically a statutory contaminated-land determination.

name: Radioactive contaminated land statutory guidance
fact: Radioactive contaminated land has separate statutory guidance from the non-radioactive Part 2A regime.
gate: Non-radioactive contamination evidence must not be used to infer radioactive-land status or vice versa.

name: Planning Data contaminated land dataset
fact: Planning Data currently reports 0 contaminated-land records, 0 providers and no collection attempt; origin is MHCLG-created pending authoritative data.
gate: Zero records must never be interpreted as no contaminated land in England or at a target parcel.

name: Planning Data contaminated-land consideration
fact: Planning Data classifies contaminated land as a planning consideration but the design work remains at backlog stage with unknown expected records/update frequency.
gate: Design-stage metadata is not an operational authoritative national register.

name: Contaminated Land Special Sites dataset
fact: Environment Agency data updated 7 April 2026 lists Part 2A Special Sites designated up to 31 December 2025 and records that some designations have been terminated.
gate: Historic designation must be checked for current status; absence from the list does not mean no contamination.

name: Oxford Land Quality Strategy
fact: Oxford explains strategic inspection, risk prioritisation and that legally determined contaminated land is entered on the public register after determination/remediation actions.
gate: Potentially contaminated history is not the same as a legal Part 2A determination.

name: Chichester contaminated land
fact: Chichester states a significant pollutant linkage requires pollutant, pathway and receptor and notes most redevelopment contamination is handled through planning rather than Part 2A.
gate: Historic industrial use alone does not establish an unacceptable complete contaminant linkage.

name: Chesterfield contaminated land register
fact: Chesterfield explains its public register is populated after specified statutory actions such as Special Site designation or remediation notices/statements.
gate: No public-register entry does not prove the land is uncontaminated or uninvestigated.

name: North East Lincolnshire contaminated land
fact: NELC publishes a written Part 2A determination example and separately explains developer responsibilities for investigating and remediating previously used land through planning.
gate: A council contamination page or brownfield history is not parcel-specific proof without the exact determination or investigation.

name: Mid Suffolk contaminated land
fact: Mid Suffolk explains local authority Part 2A duties and that some Special Sites are enforced by the Environment Agency.
gate: Regulator identity and statutory status must be confirmed for the exact site.

name: Brentwood contaminated land
fact: Brentwood states contamination is a material planning consideration and developers must investigate/remediate and satisfy the authority that agreed remediation was carried out.
gate: A remediation proposal is not completion or authority acceptance.

name: Tunbridge Wells contaminated land inspection strategy
fact: Tunbridge Wells explains Special Site referral to the Environment Agency and notes low-priority sites may remain uninspected absent specific evidence.
gate: Low inspection priority or no determination cannot be converted into no contamination.

name: Historic Landfill Sites dataset
fact: Environment Agency historic-landfill data was updated 15 May 2026, is updated about every 6 months and may be incomplete, especially for pre-licensing sites.
gate: Historic-landfill polygon presence is not a Part 2A determination; absence is not proof no historic waste was deposited.

name: Landfill sites collection
fact: Environment Agency collection separates currently authorised landfill boundaries from historic landfill sites and uses different update cycles.
gate: A site moving between layers does not by itself prove remediation, surrender or development suitability.

name: Environmental Permitting Regulations landfill quarterly summary
fact: Environment Agency dataset updated 29 May 2026 covers permitted operational and closed landfill sites under the EPR regime.
gate: Closed status within the permitted dataset is not the same as permit surrender or unrestricted redevelopment.

name: Landfill operators environmental permits manual
fact: Environment Agency manual sets environmental-permit requirements for operating, extending, closing and managing landfill sites.
gate: Permit guidance is not evidence of a particular site's permit status or compliance.

name: Plan environmental setting of landfill
fact: New landfill proposals require environmental-setting risk assessments and a bespoke waste environmental permit before operation.
gate: A suitable planning location does not imply an environmental permit will be granted.
